journal-glowingstone-page1:
The Glowing Stone

I found it in the hollow of a quartz vein, among the ordinary crystals, where my copper pick had broken into a geode. It was no bigger than my thumb, and it shone with no fire in it. When I closed my hand it hummed, faintly, the way a glass rim hums under a wet finger.

Most geodes hold nothing of the kind. Break every crystal in them all the same: now and then one gives up a stone that is not like the others.
journal-glowingstone-page2:
I bound the first one into these pages, and the book has not been quiet since. The rest I learned by grinding.

Put a strange crystal in a quern and turn it. It does not powder as quartz does. It breaks into three seedlings, small bright shards, each humming in its own small voice.

They want to be set down somewhere, and the bare ground will not do.
journal-glowingstone-page3:
A seedling wants a cradle. Take a block of polished rock, set a chisel to it, and hollow out a basin. Any stone serves, granite or marble or chalk. Set the cradle on solid ground and lay a seedling in the hollow.

It needs no water, no soil and no sun; I tried them all. It grows in a dark cellar as well as on a hilltop, and it goes on growing while I am away.
journal-glowingstone-page4:
It grows through five stages, and you learn them by eye and ear. First a sliver, then a shard the length of a finger. Then a small crystal, and now it begins to hum. Half grown, it hums louder. Nearly grown, it gives off a little light of its own. Light is its life, I think, or life is its light; my notes disagree with each other here.

Ten days or so, by my reckoning, from seedling to ripe.
journal-glowingstone-page5:
When it is ripe it stands at full size, shines like a lamp turned low, and rings once, a single clear chime. Lift it out with a bare hand. What you hold is an Unaligned crystal: pale, nearly white, of no colour of its own.

Grind it and you have three seedlings again. Set it down and it glows where it stands. And if a cradle must be moved, break it; nothing in it is lost.
journal-glowingstone-page6:
I have filled three cradles and stopped counting the crystals, yet I do not think the stone is finished with me. It is unaligned, waiting, the way a needle waits before it finds north.

Some nights the seedling by my hearth seems to hum warmer than the one I left out in the frost. Perhaps I imagine it. But I believe the crystals listen, to fire and to frost, and I mean to learn what they hear.
